requirements.title: RANGE decimal exponent formulas
requirements.definition: For integer X, RANGE has value INT(LOG10(HUGE(X))); for real X, INT(MIN(LOG10(HUGE(X)),-LOG10(TINY(X)))); for complex X, RANGE(REAL(X)).

pending.RANGE-integer-decimal-exponent-formula: Use default integer X and assert RANGE(X)==INT(LOG10(REAL(HUGE(X),kind(0.0d0)))) with result initialized to -9; this is a portable relation among inquiries for the selected integer model. Mutate to DIGITS(X) so the formula relation fails on ordinary models.
pending.RANGE-real-decimal-exponent-formula: Use default real X and assert RANGE(X)==INT(MIN(LOG10(HUGE(X)),-LOG10(TINY(X)))) and EXPONENT(TINY(X))==MINEXPONENT(X); these are portable relations among model inquiries and model numbers. Mutate TINY to EPSILON so the relation fails.
pending.RANGE-complex-uses-real-part-kind: Use a complex variable with nonzero imaginary part and assert RANGE(Z)==RANGE(REAL(Z)) and RANGE(Z)==RANGE(CMPLX(0.0,1.0,kind=KIND(Z))); these same-kind relations avoid depending on an exact model range. Mutate to AIMAG(Z) in the oracle expression so a kind/value mismatch is detected.
pending.RANGE-model-value-processor-dependence: No portable oracle can require a particular decimal range such as 38; fixtures assert the formula and same-kind inquiry relations fixed by this unit, not an exact processor model value.
